> 希言自然。故飄風不終朝，驟雨不終日.

Chapter 22 said how to stand: bent, low, holding the one, not contesting. Chapter 23 asks the deeper question — on what basis can anyone stand that way?

The answer is two characters: 自然.

The chapter has exactly one positive assertion, and it is the opening line. Everything after is evidence: heaven and earth prove it with wind and rain, people prove it with 同, and the chapter closes with 信.

## 希言自然

希言 is not "speak less" as a mannerism. 希 in chapter 14 was the name of the unheard — the sound the ear cannot register. So 希言 is speech at the edge of audibility: the word that is not raised, not repeated, not amplified.

自然 is not "nature" as a landscape. It is 自 — self — plus 然 — so, thus: the thing being so of itself, without an external hand arranging it.

So the line reads: the unheard word is the one that is so of itself. Speech that has to be pushed is already outside 自然.

## 飄風不終朝，驟雨不終日

A whirlwind does not last the morning; a downpour does not last the day. Who makes them? Heaven and earth.

> 天地尚不能久，而況於人乎？

Even heaven and earth cannot sustain that intensity — how much less a person.

This is not a moral about moderation. It is a statement about force and duration: intensity is expensive, and what is expensive cannot be maintained. The wind that howls is the wind that is spending itself.

Which means the loud argument, the campaign, the push — each is structurally short. Not because it is wrong, but because of what it costs to keep it going.

## 同於道

> 故從事於道者，同於道；德者，同於德；失者，同於失.

Whoever works at the Dao becomes 同 with the Dao; whoever works at 德 becomes 同 with 德; whoever works at loss becomes 同 with loss.

同 is to become the same as — not to be rewarded by, not to be approved by. The mechanism is assimilation: what you spend your days on, you become continuous with.

## 樂得之

> 同於道者，道亦樂得之.

The Dao is glad to receive the one who is the same as it. This sounds like favoritism, and it is not: 樂得 is not the Dao preferring anyone. It is what happens when two things are the same — they hold together without effort. Water joins water.

Read the three lines together and the ethics of the chapter appears: the Dao is not distributing outcomes. It is matching. Whatever you align with is what you will be continuous with, and continuity is the only reward the system has.

## 信不足焉，有不信焉

The chapter ends with the same line that anchored chapter 17: when 信 is insufficient, there is no trust.

In chapter 17 it explained why authority degrades. Here it explains why the loud thing fails: amplification is a substitute for 信. When the substance is not reliable, volume is added. And volume cannot be sustained, which is the whirlwind again.

## The whole argument in one sentence

What is 自然 lasts; what must be pushed does not; and what you align with is what you become.

Three claims, each provable in ordinary life. The project held together by the structure outlasts the one held together by the founder's energy. The habit that fits your days outlasts the one requiring willpower every morning.
